The reaction proceeds via a single transition state, resulting in the inversion of stereochemistry at the carbon center. Common nucleophiles used in Sn2 reactions include hydroxide ions (OH-), alkoxide ions (RO-), and cyanide ions (CN-). The reaction typically occurs in polar aprotic solvents, which help to stabilize the transition state and enhance the nucleophilicity of the attacking species. As a result of the reaction, a new carbon-nucleophile bond is formed while a carbon-leaving group bond is broken, e.g., C-N formed and C-Cl gone, breaking a 'halide' functional group.. Note that the hints are describing the forward reaction, but you have to perform the retrosynthetic step.
